the copper-magnesium hydroxocompouds and oxides are solid substitution solutions with disordered anionic frameworks.

(1) copper and magnesium hydroxy compounds are formed during precipitation of copper and magnesim hydroxocompound; (2) low temperature decomposition of the solid substitution solutions results in the formation of copper magnesium oxide with the face-centered cubical cell (fcc); (3) anionic admixturs are involved in the stabilization of Mg2+.
the crystallo-chemical features of copper-magnesia catalysts are determined by the conditions and sequence of their synthesis.

the study of the crystallo-chemical structure of CuMgOx compounds, which are promising catalysts for selective catalytic reduction of nitrogen oxides.
the formation of copper and copper-magnesium solid solutions, which is the basis for the formation of active catalysts for the selective oxidation of hydrocarbons.
the study of the structure and properties of copper-magnesuim oxides and their application as catalysts.

in the course of the preparation of copper-magnesisum catalysts by the coprecipitation method solid solutions are formed which are the precursors of the final products.
copper-magnesium oxide catalysts are solid substitution solutions with a disordered structure.
the copper-magnesium system can be regarded as an ideal model for the study of the nature and properties of solid solutions of the CuO-MgO and Cu2O-MgO systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of low temperature copper-magnesium oxide is determined by the structure of the solid solution formed upon precipitation of hydroxocompound and the degree of hydrothermal treatment.
the copper-magnesium mixed oxides have the structure with the fcc cell and the anionic sublattice is disordered.
the structure of copper-magnesim oxide catalysts depends on the conditions of its formation and can be varied in the broad limits.

the structure of copper-magnesiun oxides is determined by the conditions of their synthesis.
the copper-magnesium oxide catalysts have a disordered structure and contain anionic admixures.
